title: Competition and dense ranks
brief: Explain how tied values affect competition and dense ranking.
instructions: Return January paid UTC 2024 category transaction totals with competition and dense ranks by revenue descending. Sort competition rank then category identity.
For paid reporting activity, include timestamps at or after 2024-01-01 00:00:00 UTC and exclude timestamps at or after 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.
Return only the declared output columns, in their declared order and exact SQL types. Follow the output ordering contract; NULL ordering is explicit.
starterExplanation: This starter exposes order_id,status,ordered_at from orders without solving competition and dense ranks.

hints.text: RANK leaves gaps after peers; DENSE_RANK does not.
Compute January category totals first, then apply both ranking windows.

dataClaims.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT date_trunc('month',o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::DATE AS mon,p.category_id,sum(i.qty::DECIMAL(18,0)*i.unit_price)::DECIMAL(38,2) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items i USING(order_id) JOIN products p USING(product_id) WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND o.ordered_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' AND o.ordered_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-01-01 00:00:00+00' GROUP BY mon,p.category_id) SELECT string_agg(revenue::VARCHAR, ',' ORDER BY revenue DESC, category_id) FROM monthly WHERE mon = DATE '2024-01-01'
